skill.name: xcode-project-setup
skill.description: Configures Xcode projects by adding Swift Package Manager dependencies, linking products, and handling Firebase setup details.
skill.summary: Add Swift packages and Firebase support to existing Xcode projects with a bundled Swift helper.
skill.author: firebase

security_audit.summary: The Swift helper performs legitimate Xcode project automation, but it introduces low supply-chain exposure through remote SwiftPM dependencies and package URLs. The main confirmed execution risk is the intentional Crashlytics shell build phase, while most SKILL.md backtick findings are Markdown false positives. No prompt injection attempt or hidden data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Remote Swift Package dependencies are fetched from GitHub.
remediation.suggestion: Keep Package.resolved committed, review dependency updates, and document the expected network access before setup runs.

remediation.issue: Crashlytics setup adds a persistent shell script build phase.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user confirmation before adding Crashlytics build scripts and show the exact build phase that will be added.

remediation.issue: The helper accepts repository URLs and product names from command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Validate that repository URLs use trusted HTTPS hosts and ask users to confirm third-party package sources.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples include absolute paths inside a hidden agent directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use placeholder paths in examples and explain that users should locate their installed skill path before running commands.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Crashlytics Build Script Phase
semantic_findings.description: The helper adds a Crashlytics build phase that runs a script from the Firebase package checkout during future Xcode builds. This is expected for Crashlytics, but users should explicitly approve persistent build-time scripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code constructs a PBXShellScriptBuildPhase with /bin/sh and appends it when FirebaseCrashlytics is requested. The exact script content lives in the Firebase checkout, so the risk is persistent delegated execution rather than direct malicious code here.

content.value_statement: Adding Swift Packages to Xcode projects can be error-prone and easy to break. This skill uses a bundled Swift tool to add packages, link products, and handle Firebase plist setup.
actual_capabilities: Checks that the local Swift toolchain is available before project changes begin.
Adds Swift Package Manager repository dependencies to an existing Xcode project.
Links requested package products into the first native target framework build phase.
Optionally adds a GoogleService-Info plist file to the resources build phase.
Adds the -ObjC linker flag when Firebase products are configured.
Configures Firebase Crashlytics dSYM settings and build script support when requested.
limitations: Requires macOS, Xcode project files, and a working Swift toolchain.
Does not create a new Xcode project when none exists.
Targets the first native target found in the project file.
Depends on Swift Package Manager and GitHub availability for package resolution.

use_cases.title: Add a Common iOS Package
use_cases.description: Install a Swift Package dependency and link its product into an existing app target.

use_cases.title: Configure Firebase for an App
use_cases.description: Add Firebase products, include the service plist, and apply required linker settings.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Dependency Changes
use_cases.description: Use the same Swift helper to avoid fragile manual edits to Xcode project files.

prompt_templates.title: Add One Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a common dependency.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Alamofire to my existing Xcode project and link it to the app target. Check the project first and explain any required confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Add Firebase Core Products
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate Firebase setup with a plist file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure FirebaseCore and FirebaseAuth in my Xcode project. Use the existing GoogleService-Info plist and verify the required linker settings.

prompt_templates.title: Repair Package Linking
prompt_templates.scenario: Diagnose a project where the package exists but products are not linked.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my Xcode project setup for the requested Swift Package. Link any missing products without duplicating existing dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Crashlytics
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced Firebase setup with build settings and run script support.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add FirebaseCrashlytics to my app target, configure dSYM settings, and tell me before adding any build script phase.

output_examples.input: Add Alamofire to an existing app project.
output: The project is checked for a valid Xcode project file.
The Swift helper adds the Alamofire package dependency.
The Alamofire product is linked to the app target.

output_examples.input: Add FirebaseAuth with the service plist.
output: The Firebase package is added to the project dependency list.
FirebaseCore and FirebaseAuth are linked to the target.
The service plist is included in the resources build phase.
The Firebase linker flag is added when it is missing.
The project debug information format is set for dSYM generation.
A Crashlytics build phase is added only when it is not already present.
Existing package products and build phases are skipped to avoid duplicates.

best_practices: Review project diffs after the helper modifies an Xcode project file.
Confirm package repository URLs and versions before adding dependencies.
Back up or commit the project before running package setup commands.
anti_patterns: Do not use raw text editing to patch Xcode project files.
Do not run setup against a directory without an existing Xcode project.
Do not add unreviewed package repositories or products to production apps.

faq.question: Does this skill create a new Xcode project?
faq.answer: No. It expects an existing Xcode project or workspace created in Xcode.

faq.question: Why does it require Swift?
faq.answer: The bundled helper is a Swift Package that edits the project through XcodeProj APIs.

faq.question: Can it add non-Firebase Swift Packages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can add a Swift Package URL and link named products to the target.

faq.question: Does it edit project files directly?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper writes changes to the Xcode project file through a structured library.

faq.question: How does it handle Firebase plist files?
faq.answer: It can add the plist file reference and include it in the resources build phase.

faq.question: What should I review after running it?
faq.answer: Review package references, linked products, build settings, resources, and any added build script phase.
